subject: Monthly service signal briefing — dashboard stitch & OKR traction
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Monthly service signal briefing — dashboard stitch & OKR traction

Team — attaching the consolidated monthly service signals dump (latency / cost / uptime / usage) and a compact OKR traction CSV. High-level asks up front: 

1) Please review the latency heatmap (page 4) and flag any probe-level anomalies by EOD.
2) Confirm owners for the three items under "OKR risk" (latency p95, cache hit ratio, reserved capacity burn-down) — I suggested tentative owners in column D of the CSV.
3) I want a one-paragraph note from each of you by 3pm PT describing the mitigation we’ll present at QBR (what’s ship-ready vs. experimental).

Key signals in the deck: 
- Latency: p95 increased 12% month-over-month; concentrated in APAC region (batching scheduling window mismatch).
- Cost: token-unit spend up ~8% after the model upgrade; partial offset from prefix caching but room to tighten quantization profile.
- Uptime: internal SLOs met, but one incident window (2028-08-03) shows degraded routing fallback causing 7m increased TTFB for some customers.
- Usage: healthy organic growth; top-10 customers drove 45% of request volume.

Attachments: monthly-service-signals-2028-08.pdf, okrs-traction-delta-2028-08.csv

Irene
Irene Choi
VP, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 10:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Monthly service signal briefing — dashboard stitch & OKR traction

Irene — quick read here, two quick notes: 

- Latency spike: confirmed the APAC p95 increase is correlated with a scheduler regression we pushed in the 2028-07-30 deploy. Root cause: a fallback path that bypassed the continuous-batching queue under high-concurrency conditions. I have an owner on a hotfix (Sami) and expect a canary out by tomorrow morning.

- Incident window 2028-08-03: that was the routing-fallback loop between primary regional pool and cold-standby. We froze the pool and the circuit breaker reset at 03:12 UTC; engineering postmortem is in progress.

Actions I’ll take before 3pm PT: 
- Deliver a one-paragraph mitigation summary for QBR (owner: Markus).
- Add a short appendix to the dashboard with the canary plan and expected p95 improvements.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sarah Mitchell <sarah@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 13:30:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Monthly service signal briefing — dashboard stitch & OKR traction

Thanks — reviewed and added a few cost-focused notes inline. TL;DR: short-term cost delta from model upgrade looks to be from two sources: increased sequence length on a small cohort (finance workload) and reduced quantization efficiency for the 8-bit path.

Proposed mitigations (QBR-ready):
- Immediate: tighten sequence-length guardrails on the finance cohort (+ owner: Marissa). Estimated cost impact: -3% within two weeks.
- Near-term: re-evaluate quantization profiles and run perf regression on canary nodes (+ owner: Research Ops).
- Medium: gated rollback plan if net unit-cost increase exceeds 6% by the end of next sprint.

About the OKR ask: I retain the "cost per 1k tokens" target for this cycle but recommend we mark the quantization work as "priority 2" — we can present the canary plan at QBR as a soft-win rather than a required deliverable.

Forwarding note: Sarah — sharing the top-level signals since Acme's integration saw a marginal latency uplift; your engineering team may want to validate sequencing on their side.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Monthly service signal briefing — dashboard stitch & OKR traction

Thanks all — appreciate the quick turn. Final decisions and owners for QBR slide deck: 

- Latency p95 (APAC): owner Markus Klein — canary hotfix scheduled; prepare 2-slide appendix (one with measured p95 pre/post, one with rollout/rollback criteria). Delivery: Markus by 2028-08-17 11:00 PT.
- Cache hit ratio: owner Laura Bennett — review cache keying and cold-miss curve; bring a short remediation proposal. Delivery: Laura by 2028-08-18 10:00 PT.
- Cost per 1k tokens: owner Marissa Cole — implement sequence-length guardrail for finance cohort and provide projected unit-cost delta. Delivery: Marissa by 2028-08-18 16:00 PT.

Action items: 
- Each owner: one-paragraph mitigation + expected metric delta (numbers preferred) by the deadlines above.
- I will stitch the finalized deck and circulate to Execs (CC: CEO, CFO) tomorrow morning.
- Marissa: include a conditional rollback slide showing the threshold and customer-impact simulation.

I am copying Sarah (Acme) for visibility; Sarah, thanks if you can confirm whether your team can check sequencing rules on their QA cluster this week (no action required if not feasible).

Attachments: monthly-service-signals-2028-08.pdf (final slide 12 has the exec summary)

Irene
